tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Refresh tokens, by the application that holds them. Revoking an application's tokens makes everyone sign in to it again.
tokens.revokeDescription_one: The person it keeps signed in has to sign in to {{app}} again once its access token expires, within minutes.
tokens.revokeDescription_other: The {{count}} people it keeps signed in have to sign in to {{app}} again once its access tokens expire, within minutes.
tokens.someFailed_one: {{count}} token couldn't be revoked. Try again.
tokens.someFailed_other: {{count}} tokens couldn't be revoked. Try again.
tokens.emptyDescription: An application holds one when someone signs in to it and it keeps them signed in.
tokens.accessNote: Access tokens last minutes and aren't listed.
tokens.withoutNote_one: {{count}} other application holds no refresh tokens.
tokens.withoutNote_other: {{count}} other applications hold no refresh tokens.
tokens.grantsBefore: One person's grants are revoked in

social.title: Social
social.description: Let people sign in with an account they already have, such as Google or Microsoft.
social.offeredDescription: Each is offered on the sign-in page while it's on.
social.offeredUsed: {{n}}% of sign-ins in the last 30 days came through these.
social.turnOffDescription: Nobody can sign in with {{label}} until you turn it back on, so anyone with no other way in is locked out meanwhile. Their accounts and the link to {{label}} are kept.
social.addDescription: Each one needs an app registered with the provider, and the client ID and secret it gives you.
social.discoveryNeeded: You'll need its OpenID Connect discovery URL
social.more_one: {{count}} more that needs a discovery URL
social.more_other: {{count}} more that need a discovery URL
social.notOidc: {{names}} can't be added: Qeet ID signs in through OpenID Connect, which they don't offer.
social.removeDescription: {{label}} goes from the sign-in page and its credentials are deleted. People who used it keep their accounts and the link to {{label}}, so adding it again links them back. Qeet ID refuses while someone can sign in only with {{label}}.

form.addDescription: Create an app in {{label}}'s developer console with the callback URL below, then paste the client ID and secret it gives you. It's offered at sign-in as soon as it's saved.
form.changeDescription: Saving keeps it on or off as it is. Leave the secret empty to keep the one Qeet ID holds.
form.callbackHint: Add it to the {{label}} app's allowed redirect URLs.
form.secretHint: Stored encrypted. It isn't shown again.
form.secretKeep: Leave it empty to keep the current secret.
form.discoveryInvalid: Enter an https address, such as https://example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration.

password.title: Password sign-in
password.description: People sign in with their email address and a password.
password.turnOffDescription: Nobody can sign in with a password until you turn it back on. People sign in with a passkey, a magic link, SSO or a social account instead. Their passwords are kept.
password.rulesDescription: Checked whenever someone sets or changes a password. Passwords already set keep working.
password.editInclude: Edit what a password must include
password.alwaysRefusedValue: Common passwords, ones found in known data breaches, the person's own email address, and runs such as 12345678 or aaaaaaaa
password.alwaysRefusedHint: The same for every organisation on Qeet ID.
password.lockoutDescription: Too many wrong passwords to one account from one network lock that network out of the account for a while. People on other networks can still sign in.

lockout.panelDescription: Leave a field empty to use the platform default.

window.label: Counted within
window.hint: Each wrong password within this of the last one counts.

twoStep.title: Two-step verification
twoStep.count: {{n}} of {{total}} people have turned it on.
twoStep.where: Whether it's required is set in Settings › Security.

methods.used: Used for {{n}}% of sign-ins in the last 30 days.
methods.lastMethod: It's the only way to sign in that's on. Turn on another before turning this one off: one has to stay on.

signIn.title: Sign-in
signIn.description: How people sign in to your organisation's applications, and the rules each way in follows.

mfa.title: MFA
mfa.description: Your own second step after your password: the same as My account › Security, where everyone manages theirs.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Face, fingerprint, device PIN or a security key instead of a password. A passkey can't be phished or reused.
passkeys.turnOffDescription: Nobody can sign in with a passkey, or add one, until you turn them back on. The passkeys people have are kept, and they sign in another way meanwhile.
passkeys.ownBefore: People add and remove their own passkeys in

remember.title: Remembered devices
remember.description: After two-step verification, people can choose to remember the device: it skips the second step there until it expires. A new device is always asked.
remember.turnOffDescription: Every device is asked for the second step again at its next sign-in, and no new one is remembered. The ones remembered are kept until they expire, and skip it again if you turn this back on.
remember.editDays: Edit how long a device is remembered
remember.daysHint: Between {{min}} and {{max}} days. A change applies to devices remembered after it.
remember.daysRange: Enter a number of days from {{min}} to {{max}}.
remember.nowHint: Each browser counts as one device.

magicLinks.title: Magic links
magicLinks.description: People get a single-use sign-in link by email.
magicLinks.turnOffDescription: People can't ask for a magic link, and links already sent stop working. They sign in another way until you turn it back on.
magicLinks.editLifetime: Edit how long a link works
magicLinks.worksForHint: From when it's sent; a change applies to links sent after it. Each link works once.
magicLinks.emailHint: Its wording and branding are edited in Settings › Emails.
magicLinks.emailCustom: Your organisation's own wording, edited in Settings › Emails.
magicLinks.emailDefault: Qeet ID's standard wording. Edit it in Settings › Emails.

ownPasskeys.title: Your passkeys
ownPasskeys.description: The passkeys on your own account: face, fingerprint, device PIN or a security key.
ownPasskeys.sameAfter: ; changes made here show there too.
ownPasskeys.addDescription: Your browser will ask you to confirm with your face, fingerprint or device PIN.
ownPasskeys.nameHint: Leave it empty to name it after this browser. You can rename it later.
ownPasskeys.cancelled: The passkey wasn't created. You can try again.
ownPasskeys.disabled: Your organisation has turned off passkeys, so you can't add one.
ownPasskeys.removeDescription: You can no longer sign in with it. Add it again to use it.
ownPasskeys.lastMethod: It's your only way to sign in. Add a password or another passkey before removing it.

totp.title: Your authenticator app
totp.description: A 6-digit code from an app such as Google Authenticator or 1Password, asked for after your password.
totp.name: Authenticator app
totp.lineOn: Set up · asked for after your password
totp.setupDescription: Scan the code with your app, or type the key into it. Then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
totp.replaceTitle: Set up your new authenticator app
totp.replaceDescription: Scan the code with the new app, or type the key into it. Your current app keeps working until you confirm this one.
totp.replaceConfirmDescription: You'll scan a new code with the new app. The one you use now keeps working until you confirm it, and new recovery codes replace yours when you do.
totp.turnOffConfirmDescription: Its codes stop working, and so do your recovery codes. If your organisation requires a second step, you'll be asked to set one up when you next sign in.
totp.qrLabel: QR code for your authenticator app
totp.keyHint: Can't scan it? Type this setup key into the app instead.
totp.codeRequired: Enter the 6-digit code from the app.

codes.title: Your recovery codes
codes.description: Single-use codes for signing in when your authenticator app isn't to hand.
codes.name: Recovery codes
codes.newConfirmDescription: The codes you have now stop working. Save the new ones somewhere safe.
codes.saveDescription: Each code signs you in once if you can't use your app. We won't show them again.
codes.saved: I've saved these codes somewhere safe

otp.title: Your codes by text or email
otp.description: A one-time code sent to your phone or email address, asked for after your password. Each code works for 10 minutes.
otp.addDescription: We'll send a code there when you sign in.
otp.invalidEmail: Enter an email address such as priya@acme.in.
otp.codeDescription: We sent a 6-digit code to {{destination}}. It works for 10 minutes.
otp.removeDescription: Codes stop going there. Your other ways to sign in keep working.

toast.passwordResetSignIn: Password reset — sign in with your new password
toast.checkEmailForCode: Check your email for the verification code.
toast.codeSentToEmail: Verification code sent to your email
toast.codeSentToNewAddress: Verification code sent to your new address

applications.description: Your registered OIDC / OAuth relying-party apps.

oauthGrants.description: Applications people let keep them signed in.

signIn.description: Password, passwordless, passkeys and magic links.

social.description: Google, Microsoft, Apple, GitHub and more.

sso.description: SAML sign-in, SAML apps and setup links.

mfa.title: Multi-factor auth settings
mfa.subtitle: Configure TOTP, SMS, and recovery codes

setupLinks.subtitle: Let an IT admin set up SAML or SCIM without a Qeet ID account
